title: Keep the price audit trail complete

blocks.text: The shop's `PriceBook` keeps prices in cents by SKU, and Finance audits it: every change is written to a trail as `sku: old -> new`. The class was written years ago and has always passed its audit. This quarter the auditors found price changes that are not in the trail. All of them come from two newer jobs: the daily adjustment job, which calls `merge(sku, delta, Long::sum)`, and the yearly increase, which calls `replaceAll(...)`.

Finish the two `TODO` methods in `src/main/java/practice/PriceBook.java` so that every price change, whichever method makes it, reaches the trail. Callers of `merge` must still get exactly the behaviour `Map.merge` documents, including when the function returns `null`. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: merge() and replaceAll() still change the prices as before
a price changed or added by merge() is written to the trail
replaceAll() writes one trail entry for every price it changes
a merge() whose function returns null removes the SKU and records a removal, as merge() promises

origin.section: A Method Java 8 Added to a Collection Need Not Go Through Your Overrides

concepts: Methods Java 8 added, such as HashMap.merge and ArrayList.removeIf, need not call a subclass's put or remove, so a subclass that guards its mutators must override them too or wrap the collection.
